findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a rollback-safety note asserting the schema STATE after rollback: specify (a) what a reduced ticket looks like when old code encounters a new-format FILE_IMPACT event (file_impact_scope absent from state, consumers must tolerate missing key), and (b) what old code does with a SNAPSHOT compiled_state that already contains file_impact_scope/no_file_impact_reason (orphaned keys are ignored, no data loss), plus a test or fsck check covering the SNAPSHOT migration path (mirroring the managed_refs/attestations/creation_channel guard pattern at _processors.py:701–753).
evidence: Plan does not contain the word 'rollback' in any migration-safety context.

FILE_IMPACT events with new payload keys persist forever in the append-only log; old code's `process_file_impact` only reads `data.get('file_impact')` (src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:532), silently ignoring new keys.

process_snapshot restores compiled_state keys wholesale (`for key, value in compiled_state.items(): state[key] = value`, line 679); new-code SNAPSHOTs would bleed file_impact_scope/no_file_impact_reason into old-code state without any processor consuming them.

The established pattern in the codebase is to explicitly document and test the migration guard for every new key (see managed_refs guard at line 709, attestations at 718, keyring at 737, creation_channel at 753) — none is mentioned in the plan for the new keys.
T11 rubric: 'the plan must assert on the schema STATE AFTER rollback, not merely that rollback exits 0'.
findings.finding: The plan never asserts the schema/state after a code rollback. FILE_IMPACT events carrying file_impact_scope/no_file_impact_reason are in the append-only log permanently; after rollback, old process_file_impact ignores those keys, leaving file_impact_scope absent from state entirely (old make_initial_state has no such key). SNAPSHOTs written by new code carry the new keys in compiled_state; old code's bulk process_snapshot restore bleeds them into state as orphaned keys. Neither direction is specified, violating the T11 requirement to assert the schema STATE AFTER rollback.
findings.location: Approach section (no rollback discussion); Scope section (schema changes to common.schema.json / ticket_state.schema.json)
scenarios: Team deploys new code, a few tickets receive --none FILE_IMPACT events (new payload keys written to the append-only log), then a regression forces a code rollback: old code reduces those tickets and never populates file_impact_scope in state; any old-code consumer doing state['file_impact_scope'] raises KeyError.

New code runs compact on a ticket with file_impact_scope='none'; the SNAPSHOT compiled_state now permanently carries the new keys. If code rolls back, old process_snapshot restores those keys into state as unrecognized orphaned values — behavior is unspecified and untested.
